rules_text:
Rules summary Schafkopf is a trick-taking game. One full game consists of a number of hands with each player acting as the leader once. Contents 1 Objective 2 Playing 3 Bidding 3.1 Ramsch Optional 3.2 Rufer 3.3 Wenz 3.4 Geier Optional 3.5 Solo 4 Playing Objective The objective is (usually) to win at least half the card points in each hand. Cards points are: D 11 10 10 K 4 O 3 U 2 9 0 8 0 7 0 Suits are ranked: → → → Playing Each hand has two major phases: bidding and playing . Bidding During the first part of each hand, players are evaluating their hand and bidding to decide what version of the game will be played. Players bid their willingness to play their hand, and then increasing difficulty levels if multiple players are willing. Ramsch Optional This is the default game, if no one thinks they can win one of the other variants. Take the least points possible. Bonus for taking zero tricks. If this disabled in game options, the turn is skipped. Rufer The most common game. This is a partners game, but there is a twist: The player doesn’t know who their partner is. The player will offer “Rufer, with the D of a specific suit”, and whoever holds that card is the partner. Wenz Solo (1v3) game, with Unters as trump. Geier Optional Solo (1v3) game, with Obers as trump. Solo The solo game, with a trump suit of your choice (plus all obers/unters) Playing Play is as a standard trick-taking game; if Obers/Unters are trump, they are not considered their native suit. The partner must play their called D when it is lead, 'unless' they have four or more of that suit.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Jan10:  Well, I've played this 20 times.  What do I think?  Meh.  But when it comes to 5 player trick taking, I don't have a ton of options.  In particular, it's almost like Euchre.  It's nearly possible to play your hand on autopilot.  The only thing stopping you is determining who the parter is.  But often times that lasts all of one trick.  There is an often interesting decision in when to pick the kitty, but that doesn't quite make it cool enough.  Really, if you're looking for Euchre for 5, this will do well enough.

[Rating: 5/10] Overview: Schafkopf is a German 4p traditional trick-taking game that contributed to the development of Skat and is the immediate ancestor of Doppelkopf. The basic contract features a temporary alliance with a partner, while the more elaborate contracts are all solo (1 vs 3).  What I like: - I find temporary alliances pretty cool in general. Here, it's unclear who your partner is since the declarer simply calls a partner by an Ace card that they don't have.
